title: The hypercube Ramsey number has linear order
main_claim: Lemma 5.1 (lem:constant-broad-high-neighborhood): suppose a color G has a finite random tag I with laws mu_I on X of width at most n^gamma (gamma<1) and balanced average E mu_I <= K'_0/N, and each tag has at least chi N columns with d_G(mu_I,y) >= .95. Then G contains a Q_n for large n. The proof samples parent and stream data, hidden columns indexed by coarse bins, majority signs and severity, and center arrays. It uses predictive Steps 1-3 and a five-stage local-lemma conditioning of the history, a geometric height device, selection-corrected odd rows, clock sampling and posterior even rows, and finishes with Hall's theorem.

issues.description: k'_j is defined as the minimum of k_l over |l-j|<=1. At j=J, k_{J+1} is undefined because severity J+1 is high. If k_{J+1} were read as k_*, then k'_J=k_* and three things would fail: the mask contribution O(k_*) to the low record count would no longer fit under delta*k'_J, the requirement that the record count be less than eps^{-1}=e^{delta k'_J} would fail, and the history bound e^{-c_L k'_J} would no longer beat its pattern count. The intended reading, a minimum over low severities only, gives k'_J ~ K_2 m^{.05} log m >> k_* and everything closes. This is a notational ambiguity, not a gap.
issues.evidence: Low tuples around a low state at j=J only come from low neighbors with severity J-1 or J; the high neighbor is opposite-mode and uses a uniform reference. k_* = m^{.005} << k_J ~ K_2 m^{.05} log m.

coverage:
Block: 05-a-constant-broad-high-neighborhood-case.tex (all 1282 lines). It contains one formal statement, Lemma 5.1 (lem:constant-broad-high-neighborhood). The proof is organized into the following parts; each one was checked:
(1) Parents/H relation, segment density (2/chi^2)(.9)^{-q0} <= e^{q0/3}, R[u] marginal and width bounds: VERIFIED.
(2) Coarse bins and sign chunks: atom bounds O(n^{-.1}) and O(n^{-.15}); Pr(boundary) = O(n^{-.06}) <= n^{-.05}; Pr(j>=h) <= (C m n^{-.15})^h <= n^{-.13h} for alpha<.02. Padded key lists S cover all neighbor keys (coarse flip, F-sign flip with j unchanged, j+-1, J+1 -> high key); the shift b_j=u_{j+1} covers the prefixes needed: VERIFIED.
(3) Scales: M_*=m^{K_h eta+.005}, TM_*=o(J), T log n=o(k_*), T log n=o(m^{.02}), T+J=o(s), D_L=m^{.15} vs (T+j)k_l ~ m^{.1} log m, K_0 independent of K_s: VERIFIED.
(4) Step 1 (Bayes plus small-denominator bound, prior cap at interior and boundary keys): VERIFIED.
(5) Step 2 (subdensity tests, dP_K/dP_{K,-l} <= e^{a2 u s_l}, dP_K/dR[u] <= A_K^u, support/adjacency, optional-hit mass e^{-(a1+delta)u_*}): VERIFIED.
(6) States: D=8, low neighbors of a high state form one state (merging 5.5/6.5), parity recovery; record counts: VERIFIED.
(7) Step 3 low/high bounds; high-row construction (chain rule, exponential-moment negative parts, Azuma, grid composition count, minimax separation, R cap 2e^{D_H}/(sN), cost <= a4 k_c): VERIFIED.
(8) Five conditioning stages (Markov alarms, symmetry over bins and signs, pretrim multipliers, exponents e^{-c_L k'_j} and e^{-c_H s} vs pattern counts, local-lemma degrees): VERIFIED.
(9) Prior-heavy bound and the cube-rarity averages E B_K = O(1), Pr(j>J)e^{D_H}=o(1) (with alpha last): VERIFIED.
(10) Height choices: hypotheses of lem:height-selection (lambda=n^10, r=rho n <= d/4, theta>.9, sqrt m <= H); maximal-family marking argument; eligible >= lambda/3; 2n^b <= T: VERIFIED.
(11) Low-row selection adjustment (cancellation, fallback bound eps * #records, total 2 pi_l(x)); long/short comparison o(1): VERIFIED.
(12) Three scattered-moment passes (near-set fractions (2n^{-.04})^{300}, 2^{-m+o(m)}, e^{-n(log2-H(2rho))}; O(1)^n local-lemma costs; union over N <= n2^n labels): VERIFIED.
(13) Odd assignment via clock lemma (atoms, theta_0, B=2, failure exponent n^{1-.09 alpha}): VERIFIED.
(14) Even rows: z-independent mixture reference Q, F_z <= e^{a6 kn}Q, gated posterior lemma, union exp(O(n)+O(k_*)), density e^{tau0 kn}, H_1 removal with upsilon_1 > tau0/tau1, comparison mean d_v via 3/lambda tie bound, even scattered moments, Hall: VERIFIED.
The paper's own Section 3 tools (conditional avoidance, scattered moments, gated posterior, height selection, clock sampling) were read for their hypotheses only; their proofs were not audited.
sibling_notes: Section 3's height-selection lemma (iii) needs m=n^{alpha+o(1)} and sqrt m <= H; Section 5 satisfies this. The Section 5 state construction says it retains more information than Lemma lem:small-polynomial-broad-side (Section 6) will use; the Section 6 reviewer should confirm that Section 6's coarser states keep the D-bounded incidence and the coverage of the padded key lists.
